3.speaker: Player
3.text: “Leave the formalities aside, Deivid. Please take a seat.”

5.speaker: Player
5.text: “Of course. It's a pleasure to see you, Mr. Wisci.”

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: The door opened, and Deivid Wisci -- once a lecturer to me, now the Minister of Foreign Affairs -- gently made his way towards my desk.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: The door opened. Iosef and Lucian joined us for the briefing as the tall case clock hit the hour mark.

9.speaker: Deivid Wisci
9.text: “Somehow the inexplicable ebb and flow of life has led us here. To positions where we can change the course of history.”

10.speaker: Player
10.text: “Would you like some tea or water?”

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: He started coughing again. This time for longer.

12.speaker: Deivid Wisci
12.text: “Oh yes, please. Tea and water sounds nice. Thank you very much.”

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: Livia brought two cups of tea along with a glass of water and placed them on the table.

14.speaker: Deivid Wisci
14.text: “It seems you still remember how much I like tea. Nowadays it really does wonders for my throat.”

17.speaker: Iosef Lancea
17.text: “A little bumpy due to some turbulence. I arrived via a military cargo plane that landed at Lachaven International.”

18.speaker: Lucian Galade
18.text: “I took the train. It was a little slow, but I can still recommend it for the beautiful landscape. I also had the possibility to work on a couple of things during the ride.”

22.speaker: Deivid Wisci
22.text: “From what I've heard, it will be much faster in the near future when the L-1 high-speed railway is finished.”

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: The Blue Mansion in Lachaven hosted us for the important diplomacy gathering.

24.speaker: Deivid Wisci
24.text: “Ah right. Anton, I am used to titles, diplomacy jobs train oneself.”

26.speaker: Deivid Wisci
26.text: “Likewise. We have so much ahead of us to accomplish.”

30.speaker: Deivid Wisci
30.text: “And remember how hard we worked on the Agnolia trade agreement together?”

37.speaker: Deivid Wisci
37.text: “I still remember the first day you took my class at the Lachaven School of Economics.”

38.speaker: Deivid Wisci
38.text: “I still remember the first day you took my class at Holsord State University.”

39.speaker: Deivid Wisci
39.text: “I still remember the first day you took my class at the Deyr University of Culture.”

40.speaker: Player
40.text: “I'd rather not remember. It felt like a gargantuan task.”

41.speaker: Player
41.text: “This is our opportunity to shape the future and we will do precisely that.”

42.speaker: Player
42.text: “Countless late nights at the Ministry to finalise. It was an experience for sure.”

43.speaker: Player
43.text: “We got a little lucky. That's all.”

44.speaker: Player
44.text: “Everything happens for a reason, Deivid. It was meant to be.”

45.speaker: Deivid Wisci
45.text: “We signed our best trade deal yet with a good slew of trade advantages over Agnolia. It was even somewhat unfair from my point of view.”

46.speaker: Deivid Wisci
46.text: “That accomplishment enabled your rise in the party.”

47.speaker: Deivid Wisci
47.text: “Maybe, maybe not. I don't believe in destiny, but sometimes it feels convenient to do so.”

48.speaker: Deivid Wisci
48.text: “Our work surely contributed. Everybody made sacrifices on some level.”

49.speaker: Deivid Wisci
49.text: “I am looking forward to our new foreign policy.”

50.speaker: Narrator
50.text: He slowly sat down, taking care not to aggravate the arthritis in his knees. He'd always had an air of gravitas about him, and old age had only served to deepen that.

51.speaker: Deivid Wisci
51.text: “Oh, I haven't had any big complications except the usual... After that heart attack earlier this year.”

52.speaker: Deivid Wisci
52.text: “Yes, she has. Spending time with Margi makes me happy. There's still much ahead of her in life.”

53.speaker: Player
53.text: “Has your niece Margi started going to the kindergarten yet?”

55.speaker: Deivid Wisci
55.text: “My lovely Cathrin is as energetic as always. Age has hit me harder than her, for sure. She still does her daily jogs unlike me.”

56.speaker: Player
56.text: “So how is your wife Cathrin doing?”

57.speaker: Deivid Wisci
57.text: “The health complications aren't a hindrance to my work, of course. But thanks for asking.”

58.speaker: Player
58.text: “Monica is really taking to the First Lady role.”

59.speaker: Player
59.text: “Franc never liked the spotlight, so that hasn't changed.”

60.speaker: Deivid Wisci
60.text: “We'll talk more later, President Rayne. Welcome everyone.”

62.speaker: Player
62.text: “Let's start talking about our foreign policy.”

63.speaker: Deivid Wisci
63.text: “I sometimes wish Cathrin and I had children, but that ship sailed a long time ago.”

65.speaker: Player
65.text: “We are slowly starting to get used to the routine.”

66.speaker: Lucian Galade
66.text: “Well then. Since Mr. Vectern doesn't seem to be coming today... I think we are ready to start.”

67.speaker: Narrator
67.text: Petr, however, was missing. I wondered if he was late from all the drinking he did at the party in Lachaven.

68.speaker: Narrator
68.text: Petr arrived late. He looked a little rougher than usual. It must have been the drinking from last night.

69.speaker: Narrator
69.text: The sun began to set over the hills surrounding Lachaven. The team was ready to give advice on the new trade initiative and the response to the latest diplomatic incident with Rumburg.

70.speaker: Petr Vectern
70.text: “Hey there, folks. Excuse my delay. I'm sure I didn't miss anything we didn't already know.”

72.speaker: Iosef Lancea
72.text: “You were still supposed to be a part of this meeting. An hour ago.”

75.speaker: Player
75.text: “We are accustomed to the usual rhetoric but this is far more serious.”

76.speaker: Lucian Galade
76.text: “Punctuality is important. We are talking about serious subjects here.”

77.speaker: Lucian Galade
77.text: “A strong response to Rumburg will boost popularity at home.”

78.speaker: Narrator
78.text: The meeting concluded and the team dispersed. Our diplomatic action plan officially began.

79.speaker: Narrator
79.text: The meeting concluded and the team dispersed. Our diplomatic action plan officially began.

80.speaker: Player
80.text: “They have a point, Petr. We should have discipline in the cabinet.”

81.speaker: Player
81.text: “Petr was assigned a task from me, that is why he is late so let's move on.”

83.speaker: Player
83.text: “They are bluffing. We are used to it by now.”

84.speaker: Iosef Lancea
84.text: “I'm glad that we are drawing a clear red line. Otherwise they will keep escalating the situation.”

85.speaker: Petr Vectern
85.text: “Ah, yes, yes. It went successfully, sir.”

86.speaker: Petr Vectern
86.text: “It was a one-time thing. Let's just get on with it.”

91.speaker: Lucian Galade
91.text: “Swaying the international stage is the key in long-term strategy.”

95.speaker: Petr Vectern
95.text: “Expect a report on your desk tomorrow.”

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: Lucian and Iosef looked at Petr before Deivid moved away from the subject.

97.speaker: Deivid Wisci
97.text: “The Vice President will be part of the trade delegation, so it will be great to have his input on that subject as well as on the Rumburg incident.”

98.speaker: Deivid Wisci
98.text: “Our trade delegation will begin work towards the end of the year. We expect final negotiations and the signings of the trade agreements to happen next year.”

100.speaker: Player
100.text: “Write an official diplomatic response condemning this unreasonable act. Declare that Rumburg aims to destabilize Sordland and the region.”

101.speaker: Player
101.text: “Retaliate by closing the Sordland Consulate in Dome! They think they can bully us. They were never so wrong.”

103.speaker: Player
103.text: “We should talk about the ongoing trade negotiations with our neighbors Wehlen and Agnolia.”

105.speaker: Player
105.text: “Have a good day and enjoy Lachaven.”

106.speaker: Deivid Wisci
106.text: “Our primary goal will be to successfully sign at least one trade agreement with one of our smaller neighbors.”

107.speaker: Deivid Wisci
107.text: “Rumburg Consul Sir Bran Harrington announced the closure of the 120-year-old consulate. Now their diplomatic staff is leaving this city to go back to Thornbourgh.”

109.speaker: Lucian Galade
109.text: “He blamed the lack of security in Sordland due to the assassination and the subsequent protests. But it is obvious that they are making excuses.”

110.speaker: Deivid Wisci
110.text: “We have two options with our trade initiative. Starting new negotiations with our old partner Agnolia to the north-east, and forming a new cooperation with Wehlen to the west.”

111.speaker: Deivid Wisci
111.text: “Well, that concludes our meeting, Mr. Rayne.”

112.text: “Tell me about the trade deal with Agnolia.”

113.text: “Tell me about the trade deal with Wehlen.”

114.speaker: Iosef Lancea
114.text: “Bastards! First they close their consulate and then they blame our security!?”

115.speaker: Deivid Wisci
115.text: “I am of the opinion that it is simply too risky. Yes, we would gain resources and immediate capital, but I'm afraid of the consequences.”

116.speaker: Deivid Wisci
116.text: “As you wish Mr. President. I shall begin work by immediately informing the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.”

117.speaker: Iosef Lancea
117.text: “I want to state my support for the decision to stick to our old ally, Agnolia. Even though I disagree with their demand to relax immigration, we have cooperated with them on many issues in the past.”

118.speaker: Iosef Lancea
118.text: “I certainly don't support the decision to become friendlier with Wehlen. We carried their burdens for decades. Their migrants flooded our country and now they are expecting a deal from us.”

119.speaker: Narrator
119.text: Petr laughed. Iosef narrowed his eyes and stared at him.

120.speaker: Player
120.text: “The security situation is under control, they are playing with us.”

121.speaker: Player
121.text: “Their concerns could be genuine but this reaction is unnecessary.”

122.speaker: Deivid Wisci
122.text: “As you wish Mr. President. I shall begin work by immediately informing the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.”

126.speaker: Petr Vectern
126.text: “Isn't it telling that other countries are working with us while Rumburg is just cutting more ties with us?”

127.speaker: Petr Vectern
127.text: “Agreed. Other diplomatic missions have worked with our security units to increase the protection of staff and buildings.”

128.speaker: Iosef Lancea
128.text: “The people of Sordland must be protected, no matter the cost. I say we respond equally.”

129.speaker: Petr Vectern
129.text: “There are obviously subjects that we would still need to tackle like our economies, the traded goods and what to do with immigration.”

130.speaker: Petr Vectern
130.text: “Maintaining influence with Wehlen could prove useful. Yes, it is risky, but think about our influence on a underdeveloped region like that. We could also sell more products and enter their market easily.”

131.speaker: Petr Vectern
131.text: “I'm very much looking forward to visiting Staalport and Wraclawitz with party animals like Deivid and Symon! Haha!”

132.speaker: Petr Vectern
132.text: “Agnolia is a solid partner for us, Deivid and the President worked on the previous comprehensive trade agreement in the 30s.”

133.speaker: Deivid Wisci
133.text: “The neglect of President Alphonso, and the chaos of the elections, delayed our diplomatic efforts.”

137.speaker: Deivid Wisci
137.text: “The downside is that we would need to make concessions. A reality of any trade deal.”

138.speaker: Iosef Lancea
138.text: “I wish we had reacted more strongly. If we don't confront them, they will keep escalating the situation.”

139.speaker: Deivid Wisci
139.text: “Now there are only two Rumburg diplomatic missions left in Sordland. One is the consulate in Deyr and the other is the embassy in Holsord.”

140.speaker: Player
140.text: “I would be open to creating a new agreement that would satisfy all sides.”

141.speaker: Player
141.text: “I don't want to give any concessions to them.”

142.speaker: Player
142.text: “I think the return is too lucrative to pass on regardless of the risk.”

143.speaker: Player
143.text: “I must display strength to my people. We can't be pushed around.”

144.speaker: Narrator
144.text: Iosef Lancea was furious. He barely kept himself from slamming the desk.

145.speaker: Lucian Galade
145.text: “The migrant crisis was one of the reasons behind the destabilization of Sordland. I would like to point out that it was due to Wehlen.”

146.speaker: Lucian Galade
146.text: “Regardless, if we are going to increase our regional influence to previous levels, we might need to make amends with our neighbours.”

147.speaker: Lucian Galade
147.text: “I want to say that an escalation would be risky this early in our Presidency. We should focus on creating a negative image of Rumburg in the international scene.”

148.speaker: Deivid Wisci
148.text: “This is not the usual bluff. The military has also seen unusual build-up in the regions close to the border.”

150.speaker: Deivid Wisci
150.text: “The fact that we are headed towards a planned economy will have an influence.”

151.speaker: Deivid Wisci
151.text: “The fact that we are headed towards a market economy will have an influence.”

152.speaker: Deivid Wisci
152.text: “We either respond to this aggressive act with a diplomatic condemnation or we retaliate by closing our consulate in Dome.”

153.speaker: Iosef Lancea
153.text: “There are worrying developments like the smuggled arms and the build-up near the border. Our military must be buffed up to stand against a great power like Rumburg.”

154.speaker: Petr Vectern
154.text: “They are playing with fire. Look at what the Wehlen destabilization has done to the region. Sordland breaking apart would tear Merkopa apart.”

155.speaker: Petr Vectern
155.text: “All of this may be a calculated plan of action to push us into a corner and get us to act irrationally.”

156.speaker: Petr Vectern
156.text: “They could be. We beat them once before. They might not want to try again.”

157.speaker: Petr Vectern
157.text: “Good negotiators optimize the interests which makes the differences become trivial, allowing both sides to reach a deal.”

158.speaker: Petr Vectern
158.text: “I, on the other hand, am glad that we are taking the more cautious road.”

160.speaker: Deivid Wisci
160.text: “In my entire career I have never seen our Rumburg relations suffer this much. The previous low point was the War of Broken Wills.”

161.speaker: Deivid Wisci
161.text: “This is my fear. They might be looking for a casus belli and are slowly spiralling downward to find reasons to wage war.”

163.speaker: Deivid Wisci

168.speaker: Lucian Galade
168.text: “Exactly. If all goes well, it will be one of our major achievements.”

170.speaker: Deivid Wisci
170.text: “Look at you, Anton. The 4th President of Sordland. What a privilege for me.”

171.speaker: Deivid Wisci
171.text: “As time passes, I realize it more. Family is the most important thing in life. We must take care of them.”

189.speaker: Deivid Wisci
189.text: “Our campaign promise to steer Sordland towards the east and United Contana will have an effect on the negotiations.”

190.speaker: Deivid Wisci
190.text: “Our campaign promise to steer Sordland towards the west and Arcasia will have an effect on the negotiations.”

194.speaker: Deivid Wisci
194.text: “Especially with Wehlen. As you know the current affairs of Wehlen are partly a result of United Contana's support of Wiktor Smolak. Our promise will come in handy.”

195.speaker: Deivid Wisci
195.text: “Especially with Wehlen. As you know the current affairs of Wehlen are partly a result of United Contana's support of Wiktor Smolak. This will be a problem but definitely worth trying.”

196.speaker: Deivid Wisci
196.text: “As for Agnolia, this promise has made them cautious, which might make it harder to get a good deal.”

197.speaker: Deivid Wisci
197.text: “Since we did not promise to align with neither east nor west, it is very likely that their concerns would be more around the deal itself.”

198.speaker: Deivid Wisci
198.text: “We also need to consider the effects of our economic doctrine plan.”

199.speaker: Deivid Wisci
199.text: “Very true, Mr. Vectern. We have a lot of time to prepare before the scheduled visits to Wehlen and Agnolia.”

200.speaker: Deivid Wisci
200.text: “I believe this gives a brief overview of our current options.”

202.speaker: Deivid Wisci
202.text: “First off, the reason behind this option is more diplomatic than economic, although of course we can't forgo the added economic value. Agnolia is an old ally and a valuable trade partner.”

203.speaker: Deivid Wisci
203.text: “The point we are at with the early negotiations is around the steel trade. They are demanding that we buy their steel for a higher price. ”

204.speaker: Deivid Wisci
204.text: “Their second main demand is a privileged access to our agricultural market.”

205.speaker: Deivid Wisci
205.text: “If we are to fulfil their demands, in return they are offering a full alliance with Sordland against Rumburg.”

206.speaker: Deivid Wisci
206.text: “Obviously there will be consequences for entering a full alliance. Mainly the issue is around Heljiland. Valgsland has clear intentions on taking over the island one way or another and entering a military alliance with Agnolia will make them furious.”

207.speaker: Lucian Galade
207.text: “Ultimately the decision will be up to you as always.”

209.speaker: Deivid Wisci
209.text: “It might be unsatisfactory in the short run however, it would have real impact on the long run.”

212.speaker: Deivid Wisci
212.text: “Dealing with a fractured country like Wehlen has its positives and negatives. Although it will be lucrative in the short term, there are risks associated with dealing with such a country.”

213.speaker: Deivid Wisci
213.text: “If you decide that Agnolia is a good option, another point is that they have a very democratic system. After the recent elections the PM has a mandate to arrange a fairer deal with us. Maartin Van Hoorten also is an avid supporter of relaxed immigration.”

217.speaker: Deivid Wisci
217.text: “Since we said we will keep immigration relaxed, it will help us.”

218.speaker: Deivid Wisci
218.text: “Since we said we will tighten immigration, he might be reluctant.”

222.speaker: Deivid Wisci
222.text: “Starting the highway construction in Agnland plays a part too.”

223.speaker: Deivid Wisci
223.text: “My opinion is that this is a good deal and we should go for it. The new Agnolian Prime Minister is trying to improve the existing relationship.”

224.speaker: Deivid Wisci
224.text: “They are proposing co-investment projects and a no-tariff agreement. They are also offering oil in return for attracting foreign capital interests from Sordland.”

225.speaker: Deivid Wisci
225.text: “However, it is possible that there will be international ramifications of getting closer with a country like Wehlen.”

226.speaker: Deivid Wisci
226.text: “If we wish to go forward with the deal when the time comes, there is the topic of immigration to consider.”

230.speaker: Deivid Wisci
230.text: “Wiktor Smolak is a known isolationist. Our promise to tighten our immigration policy will increase the likelihood of the deal. He believes our borders need better security.”

231.speaker: Deivid Wisci
231.text: “Wiktor Smolak is a known isolationist. Our promise to keep our immigration policy relaxed will not help at all. He blames us for bringing western interests to the region. He also doesn't want his political opponents to flee here.”

232.speaker: Lucian Galade
232.text: “I personally don't like the idea of getting too close to Wehlen.”

235.speaker: Petr Vectern
235.text: “I still think we should give it a try.”

236.speaker: Iosef Lancea
236.text: “Looking at the current advances of Rumburg near our borders, having a coalition against Rumburg would prove extremely useful.”

239.speaker: Narrator
239.text: After he settled himself, he regarded me with delight, his blue eyes sparkling.

240.speaker: Deivid Wisci
240.text: “That is because they think that the deal is far too unbalanced as it is. ”

241.speaker: Deivid Wisci
241.text: “All in all, this is a very lucrative deal for us. However, we need to think about the consequences.”

256.speaker: Player
256.text: “I'm interested to hear the intentions of the Kingdom of Rizia.”

266.speaker: Deivid Wisci
266.text: “There are three trade-related topics to address today. Which topic should we tackle first?”

280.speaker: Deivid Wisci
280.text: “In 1918, King Egmund signed a trade deal with Queen Lyza 'the Great' to save the Kingdom from economic collapse with the support of his key advisors.”

281.speaker: Deivid Wisci
281.text: “Yes, the Rizian gold invested in Sordland in exchange for different degrees of ownership of state assets strengthened the currency by boosting the Central Bank reserves and averted a full depression after the '51 Recession.”

283.speaker: Player
283.text: “I don't need any further information about Rizia.”

288.speaker: Player
288.text: “Let's discuss the deal potential and what's on the table.”

289.speaker: Player
289.text: “I'd like to know more about Rizia.”
289.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_FPnT_Listened_RiziaDesc"] == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_FPnT_Listened_RiziaHub"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn02_FPnT_Listened_TradePolicy"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Promise_TermFocus_Military"] == false) == false)

291.speaker: Deivid Wisci
291.text: “Our neutrality strategy would have been seen as positive by nations like Rumburg if we hadn't decided to retaliate aggressively.”

295.speaker: Deivid Wisci
295.text: “Our neutrality strategy might ease the tensions with Rumburg, since their primary concern is the strengthening of the superpower blocs.”

296.speaker: Deivid Wisci
296.text: “The last handful of monarchies in Merkopa are reactive against the influences of Arcasian Capitalism and Malenyevism.”

298.speaker: Deivid Wisci
298.text: “King Romus is interested in increasing energy independence and diversifying his energy assets. Our sources indicate that he wants to acquire control of more natural gas resources.”

299.speaker: Player
299.text: “I'm cynical about monarchies. Their time in Merkopa seems to be running out, and their stability is in question.”
299.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_University_Political_Socialist"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Promise_Diplomacy_East"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_FPnT_Consulate_Retaliate"] == true) == false

300.speaker: Player
300.text: “We are still facing the potential of a recession. New avenues for trade could help keep our books balanced.”

301.speaker: Player
301.text: “Isn't this unusual? Aren't you and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in charge of arranging negotiations?”

302.speaker: Iosef Lancea
302.text: “The Toras and Livingston families should be considered allies for the time being. However, from a practical standpoint, they are too far from each other to provide military support.”

303.speaker: Petr Vectern
303.text: “Classic Wild Gus. Even before we started campaigning, he was in the game non-stop. Gus, connecting people.”

304.speaker: Lucian Galade
304.text: “Self-reliant monarchies like Rumburg are much more likely to last. But for the time being, many of the international monarchs have close ties and trade with each other to avoid revolution and change.”

305.speaker: Deivid Wisci
305.text: “Both countries are also part of the worldwide network of monarchies known as GRACE. The framework is mostly financially and politically motivated due to the pressures of Malenyevism and democracy.”

306.speaker: Deivid Wisci
306.text: “Rizia is a developed nation with a resilient economy thanks to its gold wealth. They can aid Sordland's economic health and the fiscal pain points Minister Holl keeps highlighting.”

307.speaker: Deivid Wisci
307.text: “Usually, yes, but in special scenarios such as this, real and close connections between people can improve the likelihood of a positive outcome. Since Mr. Manger has the strongest relations with the envoy, we have assigned staff to him to help with the talks.”

308.speaker: Deivid Wisci
308.text: “The international web of monarchies and sympathizers across all the continents of Merkopa, Rika, Xina, Contana have united under The Guild of Royal Allies for Commercial Exchange.”

309.speaker: Iosef Lancea
309.text: “We must take into account Rizia’s blood ties and de facto alliance with Rumburg. The King married into the Livingston family. Geographically, Rizia and Rumburg are too far to help each other; their only actual link is through sea lanes passing by Sordland.”

310.speaker: Petr Vectern
310.text: “I'm sure if Gus is involved, the deal will be financially viable. His connections in the business world are vast.”

311.speaker: Lucian Galade
311.text: “As Minister Holl rightfully described, we must do everything in our power not to fall into debt with an unhealthy economy.”

312.speaker: Lucian Galade
312.text: “But as long as we are getting a good offer, it doesn’t matter who officially leads the negotiation. I’m sure Mr. Wisci doesn’t mind.”

314.speaker: Lucian Galade
314.text: “Regardless, ideological or political motivations are less of a concern. We need to assess what Sordland stands to benefit from a potential agreement.”

315.speaker: Iosef Lancea
315.text: “If Rizia wants to buy more than 20 percent of shares allowed by the protectionism laws, then the government can step in to make changes to the EPA.”

316.speaker: Lucian Galade
316.text: “Precisely, but we don’t know if this will be the case. There is a scenario in which they might invest within the EPA limitations; we just have to hear more before weighing the options.”

317.speaker: Iosef Lancea
317.text: “The military should also be funded appropriately if additional resources are to be acquired.”

321.speaker: Deivid Wisci
321.text: “We have no close contacts with the Toras royals anymore. It leaves us little option but to use the back channel of Mr. Manger and President Alphonso.”

324.speaker: Deivid Wisci
324.text: “Ah, yes, Mr. President. Excuse me. Former President Alphonso.”

326.speaker: Deivid Wisci
326.text: “From what we have gathered, there is no clear offer yet. The interest clearly seems to be more control over the gas produced and sold in Sordland. I suspect this must be related to the recent tensions on the coast of Pales.”

327.speaker: Petr Vectern
327.text: “That must be related to Gasom operations. Gus has ties with the people around that corporation. Even though there is another CEO, Ewald Alphonso is still chairman.”

328.speaker: Lucian Galade
328.text: “I suspect that the corporation isn’t doing too well, and they are seeking investments. Any investment into Gasom will enrich the owners but might also lead to more jobs and growth.”

333.speaker: Deivid Wisci
333.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_University_Political_Socialist"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Promise_Diplomacy_East"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_FPnT_Consulate_Retaliate"] == true) == false

334.speaker: Player
334.text: “Why deal with a monarchy? They've sucked enough blood from the people of Merkopa.”

336.speaker: Deivid Wisci
336.text: “From a humanistic standpoint, without the general population participating in governance, equality problems arise. Yet these countries are here to stay.”

337.speaker: Deivid Wisci
337.text: “Mr. Manger is working out the details to get more concrete headline terms soon. Of particular interest are the gas fields in the Narbel area of the Nargis region.”

338.speaker: Player
338.text: “We should protect our energy independence, but we don’t know the offer's specifics yet.”

339.speaker: Player
339.text: “Affluent Sords don’t stray far from each other.”

340.speaker: Player
340.text: “The shareholder links raise questions regarding Alphonso and Manger's motivations.”

341.speaker: Deivid Wisci
341.text: “I agree, but Gasom is a private corporation. Even though it mostly supplies the government, we have little control over it.”

342.speaker: Petr Vectern
342.text: “Why would they? Similar circles, similar educational background, companies. Half of the oligarchs are from LBS or Harcard.”

343.speaker: Lucian Galade
343.text: “Gasom is a private corporation, a fact that limits our control over any foreign investment. Tarquin Soll's Energy Protection Act of 1932 specifically limits the purchases of Sordish energy company shares by foreign nations to ten percent.”

344.speaker: Iosef Lancea
344.text: “As a sovereign nation, we must protect our resources. Our energy independence is part of our national security concern here; Gasom handles most of our gas production.”

345.speaker: Player
345.text: “As long as we can improve our economy and resource extraction, we shouldn’t care much.”

346.speaker: Deivid Wisci
346.text: “I think we must act pragmatically in this case. I stand with Mr. Galade, as long as the country stands to benefit economically and there are no human rights concerns.”

347.speaker: Lucian Galade
347.text: “I have information that the CEO that replaced Alphonso is a loyalist. Alphonso still is the chairman of Gasom and the de facto key figure. Additionally, National Business Council Chairman Mikail Aven and Minister Gus Manger have shares in the company and preside over the board.”

348.speaker: Player
348.text: “I look favorably towards a potential investment from Rizia into Sordland.”

349.speaker: Player
349.text: “We will have to wait and hear more from Mr. Manger to decide.”

350.speaker: Deivid Wisci
350.text: “There is strong potential for further cooperation, and Rizia previously aided Sordland when it needed foreign help the most.”

351.speaker: Petr Vectern
351.text: “If there's one thing Gus is good at, it’s making deals.”

352.speaker: Deivid Wisci
352.text: “Thank you. Our support staff and I will be working towards the next steps soon after receiving more context from Mr. Manger.”

353.speaker: Lucian Galade
353.text: “I will assist in analyzing the political implications, Mr. Wisci.”

354.speaker: Deivid Wisci
354.text: “Our ambassador in Porte Drazon is in communication with Laurento Esquibel, the Rizian Councilor of Foreign Affairs, already.”

355.speaker: Deivid Wisci
355.text: "The nation south of Lespia is a centralized constitutional monarchy led by King Romus Toras. The grandson of Queen Lyza Toras, 'the Great', and son of King Valero Toras, 'the Frail'."

356.speaker: Deivid Wisci
356.text: “The Alphonso government signed vital trade agreements with King Romus Toras, benefitting both nations at a time of need. Attempts at further cooperation stalled out due to the King's blood ties to Rumburg.”

357.speaker: Narrator
357.text: Petr pulled out the ornamental coin and put it on the table. It was so polished that it caught reflections of light in the room. Lucian was clearly frustrated.

358.speaker: Lucian Galade
358.text: “The kingdom is a developed nation that wielded considerable influence in Southern Merkopa before the reign of Valero. The country has lost some territory due to internal strife.”

359.speaker: Deivid Wisci
359.text: “There is some tension with both. It appears that since Lespia's acceptance into ATO in 1950, most of South Merkopa has been heading towards a boiling point."

360.speaker: Deivid Wisci
360.text: “In the 1930s, King Romus married Princess Lena Livingston, the youngest daughter of King Alfred Livingston the Second, sister of Queen Beatrice Livingston.”

361.speaker: Player
361.text: “What exactly are these blood ties between Rizia and Rumburg?”

362.speaker: Player
362.text: “I’m curious how our neighbors Lespia and Wehlen get along with Rizia.”

363.speaker: Petr Vectern
363.text: “Actually, a friend of Gus called Rusty gifted me this beautiful piece of full Rizian gold coin. They say it helps you find love. Look.”

365.speaker: Player
365.text: “Not bad. You can't go wrong with gold.”

366.speaker: Narrator
366.text: Petr interjected and reached in his pocket.

369.speaker: Lucian Galade
369.text: “It was a political marriage that benefitted Rizia, helping save it from downfall. The two nations are close, to say the least.”

370.speaker: Petr Vectern
370.text: “All these kings and queens disagree more than agree, but they're forced to tolerate each other's differences. Imagine if Koronti and the SBC cast the world's remaining monarchs in a soap opera.”

371.speaker: Player
371.text: “I would watch the hell out of that.”

373.speaker: Deivid Wisci
373.text: “This new engagement regarding the Rizian investment interest is coordinated through our Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development, Gus Manger, and former President Alphonso.”

374.speaker: Deivid Wisci
374.text: “Many are not official allies, but have economic pacts to secure global independence.”

375.speaker: Player
375.text: “The Kingdom was meant to collapse. Nothing could save it, regardless of the effort.”

376.speaker: Player
376.text: “Your father was truly a great man, may he rest in peace.”

377.speaker: Player
377.text: “In the Tarquin Soll period, we never saw such dependency on foreign nations.”

378.speaker: Lucian Galade
378.text: “Looking a few years back, they played a significant role in helping Sordland avoid depression. There is merit to this fact.”

379.speaker: Deivid Wisci
379.text: “Former President Alphonso signed trade agreements with King Romus Toras of Rizia. The previous government revived the older relationship that existed during the days of the Sordish monarchy."

380.speaker: Lucian Galade
380.text: “Yes, with the exceptionally successful SSC bills, the Soll government raised funds for its autarky plans from the Sordish population alone.”

381.speaker: Iosef Lancea
381.text: “The Colonel knew the real intentions of foreign powers. Our strength comes from within. Our greatest resource is our people.”

383.speaker: Deivid Wisci
383.text: “Independence is important, but as the world is changing and our continental blocs are trading more with one another, we must adapt. There is a place for trade and co-development with nations like Rizia.”

384.speaker: Deivid Wisci
384.text: “Thank you, Anton. I hope our nation never faces the tragedies of those dark days again. He was the best father one could have wanted.”

385.speaker: Narrator
385.text: The room went silent for a moment.

387.speaker: Lucian Galade
387.text: “King Egmund was far too isolated and detached. Figures like Heron Walt and Artor S. Wisci spent a great deal of effort attempting to bring him to his senses.”

388.speaker: Deivid Wisci
388.text: “Times change, and any good leader must make an effort to adapt. The Kingdom indeed had structural flaws that led to the Republic my father founded.”

389.speaker: Iosef Lancea
389.text: Our Republic stands on firmer footing despite these recent troubles than those days.”

390.speaker: Deivid Wisci
390.text: "Edith Agnoc's handling with the Central Bank measures to prevent the depression also deserves credit."

391.speaker: Lucian Galade
391.text: “The relationship between Rizia and Wehlen is more complex than that. They were closely aligned under Valero's rule until Rumburg entered the play.”

392.speaker: Iosef Lancea
392.text: “Not to mention Wehlen's struggles with the BFF, an organization that we've long suspected to be armed by King Romus' in-laws in Rumburg.”

393.speaker: Player
393.text: “We have enough issues to figure out; we can’t worry about the problems of others.”

394.speaker: Player
394.text: “Merkopan geopolitics are a complexity of another caliber.”

395.speaker: Deivid Wisci
395.text: “My job is to make sense of it. It is a privilege I enjoy, regardless of my age.”

398.speaker: Narrator
398.text: At the center was the emblem of Rizia, a fierce bull standing on two feet with its horns pointed upwards. In the background was a shield intricately ornamented with leaves and a crown.

399.speaker: Narrator
399.text: At the bottom, the letters RRG were engraved.

402.speaker: Petr Vectern
402.text: “Thanks. Maybe I'll turn it into a golden tooth when I get old.”

403.speaker: Petr Vectern
403.text: “It's Rizian Royal Gold. The company that mines and processes the high-quality ore used to mint the country's gold.”

405.speaker: Deivid Wisci
405.text: “Some Rizians who settled for the deal in the final years of Kingdom still live in the Old Town of Holsord to this day.”

406.speaker: Deivid Wisci
406.text: “It's good to be informed in the diplomacy field. There is always so much movement.”

407.speaker: Deivid Wisci
407.text: “I think this summarizes all we know and what we stand to gain, Mr. President. What are your thoughts?”

408.speaker: Deivid Wisci
408.text: “I’m curious how it will develop. It’s mostly out of the hands of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for now.”

409.speaker: Narrator
409.text: Deivid hesitated for a brief moment.

410.speaker: Deivid Wisci
410.text: “The main negotiator was my father, former president Artor S. Wisci, who, with the Republican faction of the King’s parliament, fought to achieve a rare consensus in the heavily fractured council at the time.”

412.speaker: Lucian Galade
412.text: “It wouldn't be bad to focus on the important job of keeping our farmers and rural population happy.”

423.speaker: Deivid Wisci
423.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Birthplace_Lachaven_Rich"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Studyplace_Lachaven_Economics"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_EnT_Economy_Market"] == true) == false

424.speaker: Lucian Galade
424.text: “Ewald Alphonso adjusted this law in 1948 and increased it to up to 20 percent. Anything above that requires us to change the Energy Protection Act. Ewald holds most of Gasom's cards in his hands still.”

425.speaker: Player
425.text: “Remember campaigning for him back in the day? He wouldn't have gotten the USP leadership without us.”

426.speaker: Player
426.text: “Things didn't end amicably between us. I mean, we aggressively destroyed his campaign team one by one.”

427.speaker: Player
427.text: “He was right to open up the country, regardless of what happened in '51. Sordland is in a good position to benefit from world trade.”

428.speaker: Player
428.text: “I see a strong case for Tarquin Soll's regulation. Energy security is important for our nation.”

429.speaker: Player
429.text: “Gasom is private, but it still sells most of the gas it produces to Sordland, right?”

433.speaker: Player
433.text: “The way we publicly embarrassed him on national television won't help further dialogue.”

434.speaker: Player
434.text: “Good thing, we handled the transfer of power within the party diplomatically. I'm sure he will be more open to talk.”
434.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_Takeover_Backstab"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_Takeover_PublicBlame"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_Takeover_Diplomatic"] == true)

435.speaker: Iosef Lancea
435.text: “His decision not to increase the armed forces budget for the term was unprecedented. President Soll would always fund our troops a little more.”

436.speaker: Lucian Galade
436.text: “We had to break the status quo to get into government ourselves. I always thought Alphonso was too optimistic about his grand plans.”

437.speaker: Deivid Wisci
437.text: “We helped him get to power, but also led him to his fall. Such a peaceful transition with the '53 elections, however, showed the strength of our democracy.”

438.speaker: Petr Vectern
438.text: “I've got to say his team was great to work with. Toppling Tarquin Soll was a historic moment in the USP.”

442.speaker: Iosef Lancea
442.text: “Fueling the Rumburg war machine is indisputably wrong.”

443.speaker: Lucian Galade
443.text: “Up to 70 percent goes to Sordland. This used to be higher, but international demand has seen Gasom diversify its deliveries outward.”

444.speaker: Deivid Wisci
444.text: “Rumburg and Lespia are increasing their demand each year. They have hungry industries waiting to be fulfilled.”

445.speaker: Petr Vectern
445.text: “I think so, yes. Lucian knows more than me.”

446.speaker: Iosef Lancea
446.text: “This is why I like to stay out of politics.”

447.speaker: Lucian Galade
447.text: “We reached a successful result and won over the country. The rest is history; it happened. I’m focused on the history we are writing now.”

448.speaker: Deivid Wisci
448.text: “I played little to no part in the last period except for campaigning and helping Anton get the votes.”

449.speaker: Petr Vectern
449.text: “It wasn’t my preferred method, Anton, but it worked. I have to say all the bribing, persuading and promise-making we did was exhausting, not to mention expensive.”

450.speaker: Iosef Lancea
450.text: “The Sordish Council of Radio and Television should prevent disrespectful language, especially towards our elected leaders.”

451.speaker: Lucian Galade
451.text: “Any good politician wouldn't let that stop them from making a beneficial deal.”

452.speaker: Deivid Wisci
452.text: “It’s good to have a free and democratic debate in front of the eyes of the people. Even though television ownership still isn't the majority, plenty of radio listeners tuned in.”

453.speaker: Petr Vectern
453.text: “Any political opponent would have done what we did. There was too much chaos after '51, and everything weakened Alphonso.”

454.speaker: Iosef Lancea
454.text: “I would still be wary of his and Mr. Manger's intentions.”

455.speaker: Lucian Galade
455.text: “I wouldn't be surprised if Alphonso would be willing to concede more due to this fact.”

456.speaker: Deivid Wisci
456.text: “Diplomacy is the way, 99 percent of the time.”

457.speaker: Petr Vectern
457.text: “Yeah, so many people in the party approached me and praised our course of action. They thought the USP was fractured enough and didn't need further tension.”

458.speaker: Iosef Lancea
458.text: “I think it would be wise to remember that after the civil war, all the global and regional powers wanted a piece of Sordland. Like sharks in the Antacean Sea.”

459.speaker: Lucian Galade
459.text: “I wouldn't say it worked, Petr. Sordland will truly start working under our leadership very soon.”

460.speaker: Deivid Wisci
460.text: “Such is the nature of geopolitics. Our national self-interest should be preserved with as little damage done to human dignity and rights as possible.”

461.speaker: Petr Vectern
461.text: “I agree with you, Anton, and I'll always support you, but you know my motto. If something works, don't break it.”

462.speaker: Iosef Lancea
462.text: “No matter how much people criticize Soll these days, the Colonel is the reason why Sordland can stand mostly independent in this age."

463.speaker: Lucian Galade
463.text: “They smelled weakness, and thanks to initiatives of the Soll government, and the technocrats, the nation survived those hardships.”

464.speaker: Deivid Wisci
464.text: “The energy topic is gaining importance again with the tensions in the Antacean Sea. I'm keeping a close watch on the situation.”

465.speaker: Petr Vectern
465.text: “We don't want to find ourselves in the energy crisis situation of the early 1930s, where nations like Rumburg and Lespia leeched off our weakened position and charged us triple the cost per cubic ton.”

466.speaker: Narrator
466.text: Lucian pulled out a pen and took a few notes.

467.speaker: Deivid Wisci
467.text: “From our diplomatic channels, we can tell that Lespia is still very interested in Sordish petrol, whereas Rumburg wants more gas resources.”

468.speaker: Deivid Wisci
468.text: “I try to tread that difficult path to the best of my ability.”

469.speaker: Narrator
469.text: Deivid coughed a bit and then continued talking.

470.speaker: Narrator
470.text: The room went silent and no one stepped forward. It was noticeable how much people respected Wisci. He carried the soul of Sordland as a symbol of the past.

472.speaker: Player
472.text: “The power structure behind the scenes shouldn't matter much to us.”

473.speaker: Player
473.text: “Anytime Rumburg enters the 'play', crap hits the fan.”

474.speaker: Player
474.text: “I doubt he would allow it. It might hurt his hotel businesses around Port Grim.”

475.speaker: Player
475.text: “Well, we can continue official dialogue after this. It might lead to a more substantial agreement.”

476.speaker: Deivid Wisci
476.text: “Alphonso's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Keres, coordinated the previous trade agreement, but is no longer working at the Ministry.”

477.speaker: Deivid Wisci
477.text: “Of course, we are pushing to establish a stronger relationship. But in the short term, this method is the one that could yield results.”

478.speaker: Petr Vectern
478.text: “Haha! One way to put it, Mr. President.”

479.speaker: Narrator
479.text: Petr kept grinning. The rest of the room wasn't feeling it.

484.speaker: Player
484.text: “You should bring it up next time you see him, see what he says.”

486.speaker: Petr Vectern
486.text: “Well, I'd watch the hell out of it.”

487.speaker: Petr Vectern
487.text: “Speaking of movement, have you seen the latest numbers of refugees from Wehlen?”

488.speaker: Petr Vectern
488.text: “I heard Smolak also makes sense of things with certain substances.”

489.speaker: Iosef Lancea
489.text: “We didn't do a good enough job guarding our borders. Now this is causing significant tension that could lead to further friction down the line.”

493.speaker: Player
493.text: “Allowing more market economics to determine the value and output of our energy is aligned with our economic plan.”

494.speaker: Iosef Lancea
494.text: “A potential mistake when our traders use our dependence on them against us.”

495.speaker: Deivid Wisci
495.text: “I concur with Mr. Lancea. This is a distinct possibility.”

496.speaker: Deivid Wisci
496.text: “We are at a much stronger position to negotiate either way. Lucian's information gives us an extra edge in talks.”

497.speaker: Petr Vectern
497.text: “They never revealed much about their involvement to me, but I always had the feeling that Alphonso's crew was more linked to Gasom than they seemed.”

501.speaker: Player
501.text: “Keeping close control over critical resources is in sync with our planned economy strategy.”

502.speaker: Iosef Lancea
502.text: “I'm very glad you have chosen a Sordland-centric path, Mr. President.”

503.speaker: Deivid Wisci
503.text: “In theory, centralization works. But it leaves little room for outside help when internal conditions are dire.”

504.speaker: Player
504.text: “You don't need help finding love. You've got Evelyn, right?”

507.speaker: Deivid Wisci
507.text: “GRACE has proven more resilient than the international community expected. Rumburg protects the sovereignty of many of these nations.”

514.speaker: Deivid Wisci
514.text: “I am excited to present you the latest bill I am working on. The TCPA has turned out to be an initiative that may significantly boost our tourism and culture industry.”

515.speaker: Deivid Wisci
515.text: “This untapped value would help us promote our position internationally. I am convinced it can also help improve our economic condition after discussions with Ministers Holl and Manger.”

516.speaker: Deivid Wisci
516.text: “The GNA factions are supportive too. I really shouldn't have worked overtime hours to get it done, but I really care for the position and value of our cult-”
